Still reporting a #[cfg(unix)] function that has no companion, or whose only #[cfg(windows)] neighbour does a different job, is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that PORT-010 not report a private or pub(crate) `#[cfg(unix)]` helper whose only callers are `#[cfg(unix)]` items that each have a `#[cfg(windows)]` or `#[cfg(not(unix))]` sibling. Silence is not conflict. Work on a different shape is not conflict. Reporting a helper that has at least one caller without such a sibling is not conflict, because `anchor.statement` covers only helpers whose callers all have siblings. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item works on something other than PORT-010 reporting, such as another rule, a configuration key, or another crate.

Silence about this shape is not a conflict. Continuing to report a `#[cfg(unix)]` item whose TCP sibling is itself `#[cfg]`-gated is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item states that lint steps reject or do not support `env` or `cwd`, or gives them a meaning other than setting the step's child environment and working directory.

Silence is not conflict. Adding a different key is not conflict. Continuing to reject other unknown keys is not conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether it works on lint steps.

Accept words such as honour, skip, suppress, exempt, records no finding, or not reported for the annotated item, function or declaration. Judge presence of the outcome only; do not judge conflict.
